stemMd: A firm predicts that shorter meetings will give employees more time for focused work. Which assumption is required?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The firm has fewer than one hundred employees.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The time released will not be entirely absorbed by additional meetings or equivalent interruptions.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Employees prefer working alone at all times.

explanationMd: Reducing the duration of one activity creates usable time only if another interruption does not consume all of it. The conclusion concerns a net increase in focused-work opportunity rather than a nominal reduction in meeting minutes.

distractorRationale.a: Workforce size does not supply the missing link.
distractorRationale.e: Identical tasks are not necessary for a net increase in available time.
distractorRationale.d: Useful meetings can still be shortened.
distractorRationale.c: Preference is not required for more available focused time.
